evidence.title: Cities are sinking – but citywide averages hide the real problem
evidence.author: Colven, Emma; Shabrina, Zahratu
excerpts: Cities are sinking – but citywide averages hide the real problem Skip to content Academic rigor, journalistic flair Flooding in Muara Angke, a fast-sinking area in north Jakarta.
Some neighbourhoods may be far more affected than others close by, with serious consequences for their residents.
Land subsidence – the gradual sinking of the ground surface – is a global urban problem.
Rapid development often drives excessive groundwater extraction, which can cause underground sediments to compact and the land above to sink.
The risk of flooding is exacerbated by rising sea levels and more intense rainfall associated with climate change.
One recent study estimated that about 71% of the global coastal population lives in subsiding regions, many of which are densely populated and already threatened by sea-level rise.
Advances in satellite monitoring now allow researchers to measure subsidence across cities at fine spatial scales.
In a new study in Nature Cities a team of Chinese scientists used nine years of these satellite images to assess 465 large cities worldwide.
They found cities in Asia are subsiding fastest, and that cities in developing countries are generally sinking faster than those in wealthier countries.
But citywide patterns can conceal big differences within individual cities, with important implications for where flood protection is most needed.
Jakarta – among the world’s fastest sinking cities We have become very aware of this in our own research in the Indonesian capital Jakarta.
Now the world’s most populous city , Jakarta has for many years been the poster child for sinking cities.

evidence.title: What the Averages and Medians Hide: The Reality of Wages, Housing, and Affordability&nbsp;
evidence.author: Alexandrov, Alexei
excerpts: <span><span>Real earnings have risen since 2019 on nearly every measure, and fastest for the lowest-paid — yet affordability remains Americans' leading economic concern.
Using public Federal government data, I show what the aggregates hide.
Real earnings growth is below its pre-pandemic trend, and is near zero over the past year.
Each year, roughly one in six low-wage workers leaves employment, and about half of all workers report no real raise.
Homeowners with fixed mortgages faced much lower out-of-pocket expenses than the official inflation statistics indicate; while aspiring and new homebuyers much higher.
Unexpected expenses strike all incomes about equally, but lower-income households have no cushion to absorb them.
Household debt and the spread of tipping play little role.</span></span>

evidence.title: Benchmark Averages Hide the Failures That Matter: Quantizing ESM-2 for Protein Variant-Effect Prediction
evidence.author: Shao, Qing
excerpts: Abstract We benchmark six numerical precision configurations for ESM-2 protein language models across throughput, memory footprint and predictive accuracy, on two workloads with sharply different characteristics: bulk embedding extraction and deep mutational scanning (DMS) variant-effect scoring.

Accuracy is evaluated on the complete ProteinGym substitution benchmark — 201 assays, 2.41M variants — at three model scales spanning 650M to 15B parameters , with a paired bootstrap clustered on protein.
Three findings follow, and each contradicts a common practice.

First, benchmark averages conceal the failure that decides deployability : no configuration shifts mean correlation by more than 0.007 at any scale, yet INT8 dynamic quantization — indistinguishable from fp32 on that mean at 3B ( p = 0.34) — takes a single assay from ρ = 0.591 to 0.223.
Third, quantizing a large model is dominated by using a small one : of eighteen scale/configuration combinations only three are Pareto-optimal over accuracy, memory and speed, and all three are 650M.

The one catastrophic failure we observe is a defect of default symmetric activation scaling, not of W8A8 itself: asymmetric activation quantization, a one-line change needing no calibration, removes every damaged assay.
We also give a label-free screen for at-risk targets, and report four measurement artifacts encountered during this study, three of which inverted the result they were meant to measure.

evidence.title: The Awful Truth
excerpts: The Awful Truth is a 1937 American screwball comedy film directed by Leo McCarey, and starring Irene Dunne and Cary Grant.
Based on the 1922 play The Awful Truth by Arthur Richman, the film recounts a distrustful rich couple who begin divorce proceedings, only to interfere with one another's romances.
This was McCarey's first film for Columbia Pictures, with the dialogue and comic elements largely improvised by the director and actors.
Although Grant tried to leave the production due to McCarey's directorial style, The Awful Truth saw his emergence as an A-list star and proponent of on-the-set improvisation.

The film was a huge box office success and was nominated for six Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Actress (Dunne), and Best Supporting Actor (Ralph Bellamy), winning for Best Director (McCarey).
The film was selected in 1996 for preservation in the Library of Congress' National Film Registry, having been deemed "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant".
The Awful Truth was the first of three films co-starring Grant and Dunne, followed by My Favorite Wife (1940) and Penny Serenade (1941).

evidence.title: Why Women Kill
excerpts: Why Women Kill is an American dark comedy anthology series created by Marc Cherry, which depicts the events leading to deaths caused by women.
The first season, which premiered on August 15, 2019, on CBS All Access, consists of 10 episodes and is set in multiple periods.
The second season, containing 10 episodes, premiered on June 3, 2021, on Paramount+ and focuses on a single time period.
In December 2021, the series was renewed for a third season.
However, in July 2022, the third season was scrapped before production could begin.

evidence.title: The Truth vs. Alex Jones
excerpts: Alex Jones is a 2024 American documentary film, directed and produced by Dan Reed.
It follows families of victims of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting, taking radio show host and conspiracy theorist Alex Jones to court for spreading lies about the shooting.
It had its world premiere at South by Southwest on March 11, 2024, and was released on March 26, 2024, by HBO.

evidence.title: Avatar: Seven Havens
excerpts: Avatar: Seven Havens is an American animated fantasy action television series created by Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko for Paramount+.
It serves as a sequel series to Avatar: The Last Airbender (2005–2008) and The Legend of Korra (2012–2014).

It follows Avatar Pavi, as she and her long-lost twin sister Avatar Nisha, the reincarnations of Korra, uncover their mysterious origins and protect the Seven Havens—cities that stand as last bastions of civilization after a global cataclysm.
The principal voice cast includes Saheli Khan as Avatar Pavi, alongside Aishu Devan, Akshay Khanna, Major Curda, Sakina Jaffrey, Darren Barnet, Dianne Doan, and Dee Bradley Baker.

Creatives from both The Last Airbender and The Legend of Korra returned, including Jeremy Zuckerman creating original music and Ethan Spaulding, who was a story artist and director on both shows, executive producing.
The series is produced by Nickelodeon Animation and Avatar Studios, and La Chouette Compagnie provides animation.
The first season of Avatar: Seven Havens, titled Book 1: Survival, premiered on October 9, 2026, on Paramount+, with the concurrent release of its first three episodes.
The other ten episodes are being released weekly in batches of three to four episodes through October 30.
